title: The Fourth, 2009
logline: Three weeks married. Gully and Maria at the machine. Wood on the steps. The chair: Maria drags it out from under the eave and sits in it, and Gully lets her, and that's that.

panels.composition: The dock, fireworks white on blue. GULLY pouring. MARIA dragging the lawn chair out from under the eave into the open, sitting in it, feet up on a crab pot. WOOD on the steps. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a crowded dock at night under white fireworks, a practical woman dragging an old lawn chair out from under a shack's eave into the open and sitting in it with her feet on a crab pot, a man in an apron pouring, a thin man on the steps with a dog, muddy watercolor

panels.composition: Gully, watching her do it. Not stopping her.

image.prompt: close-up of a man in an apron watching something with a face that decides to let it happen, no words

panels.composition: Maria, in the chair, to Wood on the steps.

balloons.text: To see if you'd say it.

image.prompt: a woman in a lawn chair speaking across to a thin man on shack steps, fireworks light

panels.composition: The finale. White. The chair in the open, occupied, for good. The eave empty for the first time in nine years.

image.prompt: a fireworks finale in white over a blue night bay above a dock where an old lawn chair sits out in the open with a woman in it and the shack's eave is empty, watercolor, no words

art.line: brush-pen; the flats cleaner; Sundays the point

notes: Maria takes the chair. 'To see if you'd say it.' The eave empty.
